step1_summary.chief_complaint: Weird symptoms including tiredness, numbness, and weakness.

symptoms.onset: Started about a month and a half to two months ago.
symptoms.duration: Episodes last a few days, with increasing frequency.
symptoms.severity: Symptoms include tiredness, pins and needles, weakness, and difficulty holding objects.
symptoms.aggravating_factors: Symptoms seem to occur in episodes.
symptoms.alleviating_factors: Symptoms resolve after a few days.

step1_summary.past_medical_history: No significant past medical history; no history of mini-strokes.
step1_summary.medications/allergies: Taking aspirin 75 mg daily; allergic to penicillin.
step1_summary.family/social_history: Family history of stroke (father had surgery to reduce stroke risk); patient is a doctor in plastic surgery; lives with wife.
step1_summary.vital_signs/exam_findings: No vital signs documented; episodes of weakness and numbness in the right hand and arm, abnormal gait.
step1_summary.labs/imaging: Recent blood tests for diabetes and cholesterol were normal.

V: Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA): Symptoms of weakness and numbness in the right hand and arm, along with a family history of stroke.
Stroke: Similar symptoms to TIA but may be less likely given the episodic nature and resolution of symptoms.
I2: Aspirin side effects: While unlikely, aspirin can rarely cause bleeding or other complications.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: The episodic nature of the symptoms, including weakness, numbness, and abnormal gait, combined with a family history of stroke raises concern for TIA.
supporting_evidence: Episodes of weakness and numbness in the right hand and arm.
opposing_evidence: Patient is relatively young (32 years old) and has no personal history of strokes.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: While the symptoms could indicate a stroke, the transient nature of the symptoms makes this less likely.
supporting_evidence: Symptoms suggestive of neurological involvement (weakness, numbness).
opposing_evidence: Symptoms resolve after a few days and are not persistent.

supporting_evidence: Patient is taking aspirin for stroke risk.
